items.title: 12.9 The asymmetry of matter and antimatter in the universe

source_refs.note: Topic 12.9 (PDF 274, printed 271). The hydrogen and helium percentages differ from those given in 12.10 (68% and 27%); recorded.

blocks.text: Many observations show that there is an asymmetry between matter and antimatter; this is one of the most remarkable features of our universe. A number of observations indicate that the universe consists almost entirely of matter rather than antimatter. For example, the book describes the universe as having about 5% ordinary matter (electrons, protons and neutrons), with this matter about 72% hydrogen and 24% helium, and there is no contribution of antihydrogen or antihelium atoms to the composition of the universe.

The book states that the matter-antimatter asymmetry is due to the violation of conservation of baryon number, that is, an imbalance between the number of baryons and antibaryons. If particle-antiparticle symmetry is also violated, there would be a mechanism for making more quarks than antiquarks, more leptons than antileptons, and eventually more matter than antimatter. Hence it is concluded that the asymmetry of matter and antimatter is still a mystery.

blocks.title: An unsolved problem
blocks.text: Why the universe contains almost no antimatter is one of the great unanswered questions of physics; the explanations above are hypotheses, not established results.

blocks.prompt: Discuss reasons why our universe is almost entirely composed of matter (comprehensive question 12.3). The asymmetry of matter and antimatter is due to an imbalance in the number of which particles (MCQ 12.16)?
blocks.explanation: If matter and antimatter had been made in exactly equal amounts after the Big Bang, they would have annihilated into radiation; the matter we see means a tiny excess of matter survived. Proposed reasons are processes that do not conserve baryon number and that treat particles and antiparticles slightly differently, so that more quarks than antiquarks and more leptons than antileptons were produced; the exact cause is still a mystery. MCQ 12.16: (c), baryons.

items: The universe is almost all matter: no antihydrogen or antihelium is found (book: ordinary matter about 5%, of it about 72% hydrogen and 24% helium). Suspected cause: violation of baryon-number conservation and of particle-antiparticle symmetry; still an unsolved mystery.
